Subject: Order Form Pricing — threshold smoothing, min commitment & cap/floor language

Hi Sasha / Jordan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, attaching a redline of the Order Form pricing exhibit (OrderForm_v3_PricingExhibit_redline.pdf) with two focused asks where we need alignment before legal sign-off:

1) Threshold smoothing (Section 2.3): we proposed a 3-month rolling smoothing window to avoid cliff true-ups from brief usage spikes. Can Acme accept language that permits a single-month deviation without triggering immediate true-up provided 3-month rolling average stays within the band?

2) Caps & floors (Section 4 / Exhibit B): Acme asked to soften the floor protection. We've proposed a narrow floor to protect unit economics while offering a temporary 10% credit in months where usage falls under the floor during the first 6 months of the term — applies only to overage tokens, not committed ones.

Quick asks for you: please review the attached redline and let us know (a) whether your procurement team needs the floor fully removed, or if the 6-month soft-credit is acceptable; (b) whether the smoothing window language is operationally acceptable or if you need explicit carveouts for pilot workloads.

If helpful, Marissa and Karthik are cc'd and can provide the operational and commercial context. We’d like to lock language by EOD Friday 11/17 to keep the DocuSign timeline intact.

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear note and for the redline. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed and returned a markup (attached). High-level comments inline:

- Smoothing window: Procurement likes the intent but needs an explicit definition of "pilot workloads" and an objective cap (e.g., <1% of total committed tokens per month) for any carveout. Otherwise they fear repeated exceptions.

- Floor removal ask: Acme cannot accept a firm floor in perpetuity; we are asking for either (A) remove the floor entirely with a higher committed minimum or (B) limit the floor to the first 12 months only.

- True-up timing: Legal prefers true-ups quarterly rather than monthly to reduce billing churn.

I attached ACME_legal_markup_v2.pdf with inline comments and a suggested alternative text for Section 4 (see pp. 2–3). Jordan, please confirm procurement's comfort with quarterly true-ups and whether the pilot carveout threshold below 1% is acceptable operationally.

Team —

I reviewed Acme's markup and Sasha's asks. Suggested approach below (short, so AE can send to legal/procurement):

1) Smoothing window: accept a 3-month rolling average but add a one-line definition for "pilot workloads" ("pilot workloads = distinct workloads comprising <= 1% of total committed tokens in any given month and <= 3% of the aggregate over a rolling 12-month period"). That gives procurement the objective cap they want.

2) Floor compromise: offer Option B — limit the contractual floor to the first 9 months (not 12), combined with the 10% temporary credit for months where usage falls below the floor. That narrows Redwood's exposure while showing willingness to flex.

3) True-up cadence: accept quarterly true-ups, tied to calendar quarters, with one off-cycle true-up permitted on mutual written request (to handle obvious overages).

4) Commercial concession: to make this palatable, propose a one-time implementation credit of 10% on overage pricing for months 1–3 only (to support Acme's ramp). We should reserve additional credits for exec approval.

Please find suggested contract text below (copy-paste friendly):
"Section 2.3 (Smoothing): For purposes of determining compliance with the Usage Thresholds, a three-month rolling average will be used. \"Pilot workloads\" are defined as distinct workloads comprising <= 1% of committed tokens in any given month and <= 3% of aggregate committed tokens over a rolling 12-month period. Pilot workloads shall be excluded from smoothing calculations for up to two distinct pilot periods per 12-month window, each pilot period not exceeding 60 days."

"Section 4 (Floor): The Minimum Monthly Commitment Floor shall apply for the first nine (9) months of the Term. If Customer usage in any month during the initial nine-month period falls below the Floor, Customer shall be eligible for a ten percent (10%) credit applied to overage charges for that month, subject to the terms in the Parties' billing policy. Thereafter, the Floor shall expire unless mutually extended in writing."

If legal likes the copy, Naomi can send to Sasha. I copied Laura for finance/billing confirmation on the credit mechanics.

–Marissa

Sasha / Jordan —

Thanks for the quick review and the markup. Based on Marissa's recommended approach, Redwood can accept the following compromise to close the pricing exhibit: 

- Smoothing: 3-month rolling average with the pilot workload definition (<=1% monthly / <=3% rolling 12-month).
- Floor: limited to the first nine (9) months of the term, with a 10% credit applied to overage charges in months where usage falls below the floor (implementation credit for months 1–3 to help ramp).
- True-ups: quarterly cadence (calendar quarter), with one off-cycle true-up permitted upon mutual written agreement.

If that matches Acme's needs, we'll prepare a final clean Order Form and send a DocuSign envelope. I’ve attached a signature-ready draft (OrderForm_Final-draft-for-signature.pdf) and included the HubSpot deal and DocuSign links below for Jordan's procurement team to track.
